summary: II regularly codes the viewed person, object or event with ʕal-/aʕl-, while an understood spectacle is often omitted. Bare Infectum occurs after motion or d-; ko-/k- forms describe ongoing scenes and gə- occurs with prospective or repeated events, so no automatic temporal interpretation follows from the German tense.
Prefixless farəǧ/fareǧu occur across PrS and JTM. PrS 43/72 also has m-less faraǧǧe, unlike common mfaraǧǧe. Retain these source forms; do not create a separate stem solely from loss of m-.
PrS 6/18 concerns a flute performance. It may involve attending rather than specifically hearing; PrS 44/24 German Vergnügen likewise supplies affect not encoded separately in the verb.
The source ksoyəm fərǧe in PrS 57/69 is a nominal light-verb expression, not another frǧ finite token. Lookup search fərǧe gave no hit; no frǧ idiom is inferred from the cognate noun alone.
No new etymology is asserted for III. II has the inherited Arabic derivation; the relief use may need a separate borrowing or homonym decision.

The II Infectum-wa examples distinguish remembered watching of bear shows and a butcher from unrealized film viewing. The four selected Jan examples bring the box to five including the inherited example.
At Jan 3 kmifarəǧ and plural kmifarǧi occur together. The vowel mi- is not the t-bearing morphology of round-1 mətfarǧina, so no second Detransitive box is claimed.
Jan 3022 li fərǧe is a purpose nominal. Round 1 already identified the cognate noun in sym fərǧe; a lexical noun alone does not establish II Infinitiv.
No Jan evidence modifies round-1 III relief sense, II Detransitive proposal, source corrections or sense numbering. Those proposals are not repeated in entry.json.
89/93: confirm III ma-fraǧ-la, the function/referent of -la, the exact government, and whether relief belongs under a separate homonym. No Preterit base is supplied.
107/108: is mətfarǧina a II Detransitive variant or a separately borrowed tfrǧ verb? It has the same observer semantics as gəmfarǧina in 107/110.
PrS 6/18: can frǧ itself mean hearing, or does it mean attending/watching the flute performance?
PrS 15/90: the edition translation omits the watching clause. Supply a matching edition passage before adding this example.
Hors 2/48: confirm the feminine-address mfaraǧ and whether hano u zlamano is its unmarked target or part of the following clause.
PrS 44/67, 50/144 and 57/84: identify the singular-shaped watcher and agreement. PrS 75/90: confirm short mfarǧən person/number; JL 13.11/18 and PrS 43/72: confirm doubled ǧ and m-less variant.
Jan 3022: is fərǧe an independent borrowed viewing/spectacle noun or a productive II Nomen Actionis? No new Infinitiv has been published from it.
Jan 4.0/3: is kmifarəǧ generic singular active with vowel insertion, or an impersonal construction? Confirm before interpreting mi- as Detransitive.
Capitalize the German noun Geschichten
rationale: Geschichten is a German noun and is capitalized in the cited edition. Its lowercase initial is a typo.

summary: Observer subjects include animals and an infant; targets include landscapes and performances. Official inspection, looking without intervening and looking during a stroll remain contextual uses of watching.
Television programmes and films are viewed with the same ʕal-target coding as immediate spectacles. This is an extension of the viewed medium, not a new technical sense.
